label: sound
instruction_covers: rendering an Http404 directly, from a decorated view, or via middleware yields the normal JSON envelope: status 404, NOT FOUND status text, exception message as content
other exceptions on an AJAX request yield a 500 envelope; with DEBUG false the content is a generic safe message that discloses neither the exception text nor the traceback
a request passed for logging is accepted but never forwarded as an option to the JSON encoder
the decorator envelopes an ordinary HttpResponse using its status code, reason phrase and body
the existing mandatory non-AJAX guard is preserved, and mandatory=False passes a non-AJAX request through unchanged
middleware converts AJAX responses and exception results with the same rules, leaves non-AJAX responses and exception handling untouched, and does not nest an already-JSON response
a caller-supplied JSON encoder and standard json.dumps options keep working
notes: The exact envelope keys (status, statusText, content), the reason phrases (NOT FOUND, CREATED, ACCEPTED) and the mandatory guard returning HTTP 400 are pre-existing django-ajax conventions, present since the 2014 package rename and documented in the decorator's own docstring and the REASON_PHRASES table. The instruction points at them by name ('the normal JSON envelope', 'status text', 'reason phrase', 'existing mandatory non-AJAX guard'), so a careful engineer reads them off the repo rather than guessing. The tests never pin the wording of the generic safe message, only that the exception text and traceback are absent.
